'''David John Millener''' (born 2 May 1944) is a New Zealand physicist and former [[cricket]]er. He played 26 matches of [[first-class cricket]] for [[Auckland cricket team|Auckland]] and [[Oxford University Cricket Club|Oxford University]] between 1964 and 1970.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/37922.html |title=David Millener |accessdate=18 June 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> Since 1976 he has lived in the United States, pursuing a career as a nuclear physicist at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]].

==Education and career==
Millener was born in [[Auckland]]. His father was a lecturer in botany at the [[University of Auckland]]. He attended [[Auckland Grammar School]]<ref>{{cite journal |title=Lectures in Sydney |journal=Press |date=16 November 1961 |page=16 |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19611116.2.141}}</ref> before going on to the University of Auckland. He was awarded a [[Rhodes Scholarship]] to study at [[St Catherine's College, Oxford]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.universitiesnz.ac.nz/files/u12/New%20Zealand%20Rhodes%20Scholars%20Since%201904.pdf |title=New Zealand Rhodes Scholars Since 1904 |publisher=Universities New Zealand}}</ref> where he gained a doctorate ([[D.Phil.]]) in physics in 1972 with a thesis entitled "Shell Model Studies in Light Nuclei".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/library/thesus.asp?LID=Fisher+Room |title=Fisher Room: Thesis List |publisher=Department of Physics, University of Oxford |access-date=10 June 2017 |archive-date=7 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180107061141/http://www.physics.ox.ac.uk/library/thesus.asp?LID=Fisher+Room |url-status=dead }}</ref> He stayed on at Oxford as a post-doctoral fellow for three years.<ref name=MWW>{{cite web |title=John Millener, DPhil |url=https://whoswhonewsletters.com/2020/09/28/john-millener/ |website=Marquis Who's Who |date=28 September 2020 |access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref>

He moved to the United States to work at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] at [[Upton, New York]], in 1976.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=A Job Well Done |magazine=Brookhaven Bulletin |date=23 September 1977 |page=3 |url=https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/bulletin/1947-1995/1977/23091977.pdf}}</ref> He worked there as a physicist until 2013, when he retired from full-time work, retaining the title of guest physicist. He specialised in research in nuclear structure and [[Hypernucleus|hyper-nuclear physics]].<ref name=MWW/> In 1993 the [[American Physical Society]] awarded him a Division of Nuclear Physics Fellowship, "For significant contributions to understanding the structure of light nuclei; particularly non-normal parity states and to hyper-nuclear spectroscopy and the application of SU(3) symmetries."<ref>{{cite web |title=APS Fellows Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?award_fellowship%5Bpage%5D=136 |website=APS |access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref> He has contributed more than 80 articles to scientific journals.<ref name=MWW/>

==Cricket==
A right-arm fast-medium bowler, Millener played regularly for the Auckland [[Plunket Shield]] team between 1964–65 and 1967–68. He played for Oxford University between 1969 and 1973.<ref>{{cite web |title=First-Class Matches played by John Millener |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/22/22487/First-Class_Matches.html |publisher=CricketArchive |access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref> He represented the [[United States national cricket team|United States]] in the [[1982 ICC Trophy]] in England. His most successful first-class match was Oxford University's victory over D. H. Robins' XI in 1969, when he took 3 for 41 and 4 for 97.<ref>{{cite web |title=DH Robins' XI v Oxford University 1969 |url=http://static.espncricinfo.com/db/ARCHIVE/1960S/1969/ENG_LOCAL/UNIV/ROBINS_OX-UNIV_UNIV_18-20JUN1969.html |publisher=Cricinfo |access-date=7 March 2025}}</ref>
